llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its media-generation purpose, but it needs Review because it reads unrelated Telegram credentials and can upload arbitrary local files to external services.

dimensions.detail: Network access to RunPod and R2 is expected, but local path arguments are uploaded without directory, file type, symlink, or size checks, and returned media URLs are downloaded without host or size restrictions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no separate installer or startup mechanism, but scripts run through uv with unpinned runtime dependencies such as requests and boto3.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions direct the agent to use normal delivery first, then read a Telegram bot token from ~/.openclaw/secrets.json and call the Telegram Bot API directly if delivery fails, which is high-impact and not declared in metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can write generated media under ~/.openclaw/workspace/runpod-media and can modify scripts/endpoints.json for future endpoint use; it also accesses shared secrets beyond the declared RunPod/R2 requirements when using Telegram fallback.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: RunPod media generation and R2 uploads are purpose-aligned and mostly disclosed, but the Telegram delivery fallback and broad 'any endpoint' support expand the skill beyond the core media-generation description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill sending prompts and media to RunPod, temporarily uploading local inputs to Cloudflare R2, and potentially delivering outputs through Telegram. Review or remove the Telegram curl fallback before use, restrict which local files may be uploaded, and avoid arbitrary endpoint IDs unless you trust the endpoint and understand where the data will go.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Use of the RunPod API key in Authorization headers to api.runpod.ai is expected for this skill and is not credential exfiltration by itself.
[PE3] unexpected: RunPod and R2 secret reads are expected, but the SKILL.md Telegram fallback reads /telegram/botToken from the shared secrets file even though the metadata does not declare that credential.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The direct Telegram API fallback sends generated files outside the platform messaging abstraction and is materially broader than the stated RunPod media function.
[TP4] expected: Endpoint listing, probing, and adding are disclosed in SKILL.md, so this is not hidden tool poisoning, but registry writes and arbitrary endpoint IDs still broaden future scope and should be user-controlled.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading local media to Cloudflare R2 and RunPod is part of the workflow and is disclosed, but the lack of local-file scoping makes it risky for sensitive paths.
[SC2] unexpected: The cited curl block is not remote script execution; the supported concern is direct Telegram credential use and media transmission.
[T05] unexpected: The SARIF least-privilege concern is supported by artifact evidence: SKILL.md instructs direct access to Telegram bot credentials as a fallback delivery path.
[T09] unexpected: The SARIF local-file upload and unrestricted response download concerns are supported by _utils.py: arbitrary non-URL paths are opened and uploaded, and endpoint-provided URLs are downloaded without allowlisting or size limits.
[T08] expected: Runtime dependency resolution through uv is expected for these scripts, but the dependencies are unpinned and therefore not reproducible.
